body.text: Panel A. Logit; dependent variable: default
Panel B. OLS; dependent variable: prediction error, 100 × (default − PD), in pp
Panel C. Difference in the female coefficient, T+AD minus T

note: Final evaluation sample; 7,199 defaults. Panel A: if the model is accurate for both genders, the coefficient on logit(PD) is close to 1 and the female coefficient is 0. The average marginal effect is the mean change in the predicted default probability when the female indicator switches from 0 to 1. Panel B: a negative female coefficient means that women's risk is overestimated relative to men's; the coefficient equals the difference between women's and men's mean prediction errors. Panel C: both models' rows are stacked and the female coefficients are compared, with standard errors clustered by application. Heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors in parentheses. *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.10.

caption: Adding demographic controls
note: Logit of default on logit(PD), the female indicator and the listed controls; every column also includes logit(PD). Column (2) is the same as in Table 1. Missing family state and employment length are kept as separate categories. HC1 standard errors in parentheses. *** p < 0.01.

caption: Difference in mean feature contributions, women minus men
note: Each application's model score (log-odds) equals a common starting value plus the SHAP contribution of every input. The table reports the mean contribution of each family for women and men and the difference, women minus men; a positive difference means that the family raises women's scores relative to men's. Because the starting value is the same for everyone, the differences add up to the gap in mean scores. Change = the T+AD difference minus the T difference. The observed gap is logit(women's default rate) minus logit(men's default rate). Welch standard errors in parentheses. *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.10.

caption: Shape of the gender gap along the PD scale
note: Logit of default. logit(PD) is centred at its sample mean in the interaction, so g is the gender gap for an applicant with average predicted risk. h = 0 means that the gap is the same proportion at every risk level; h < 0 means that the gap widens as predicted risk rises; h > 0 means that it narrows. Demographic controls: age, age²/100, family state and employment length. Women's slope b + h is computed from the covariance matrix. HC1 standard errors in parentheses. *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.10.

note: Logit of default on the family components of the model score (each centred at its sample mean), the female indicator, and female × component interactions. c is the change in men's actual default log-odds when the model's score rises by one unit because of that family; c + h is the change for women, and h is the difference between the two. If the model is accurate for both genders, every c equals 1, every h equals 0 and g equals 0. HC1 standard errors in parentheses. *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.10.
